    category: "detection"

    our_advantage: "ContamCal reveals S4 ineffectiveness and integrates it into multi-signal RRF where its noise is diluted."

  - id: "golchin_2024_time_travel"
    title: "Time Travel in LLMs: Tracing Data Contamination in Large Language Models"
    authors: "Golchin & Surdeanu"
    venue: "ICLR 2024"
    year: 2024
    url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.08493"
    category: "detection"
    role: "background"
    relevance: "Proposes guided prompting to detect contamination via LLM's ability to reproduce benchmark instances. Complementary approach to our signal-based detection."
    key_findings: "Detects contamination across GPT-4, GPT-3.5, LLaMA-2 via instance reproduction; confirms widespread contamination in major LLMs."
    our_advantage: "Time Travel requires model generation access; ContamCal works with item-level responses only. Our approach quantifies effects, not just detects."

    year: 2025
    category: "mitigation"
    role: "direct-competitor"
    relevance: "Closest predecessor to ContamCal. DCR applies decontamination + calibration + ranking correction. Lacks IRT grounding, uncertainty quantification, and domain-level diagnosis. Key W1 comparison target."
    key_findings: "Score adjustment framework for contaminated benchmarks; demonstrates improved ranking consistency post-decontamination."
    our_advantage: "ContamCal provides: (1) Bayesian CIs vs point estimates, (2) domain-level γ diagnosis vs aggregate correction, (3) Fisher Info identifiability analysis, (4) Min-K++ reversal detection."

    category: "mitigation"

    key_findings: "Rephrased benchmarks show significant performance drops in contaminated models; surface-level memorization dominates."
    our_advantage: "Rephrasing prevents contamination for new evaluations; ContamCal calibrates existing contaminated scores. Different scope."

tool_args.old_string: We propose ContamCal, a two-stage post-hoc calibration framework for contamination-adjusted benchmark scoring. In Stage~1 (\emph{Multi-Signal Provenance Mapping}), four training-free detection signals---embedding-based near-duplicate retrieval, Min-K\%++ membership inference, ConStat performance gaps, and Self-Critique entropy collapse---are aggregated via reciprocal rank fusion \citep[RRF;][]{cormack2009} to produce per-item exposure scores. RRF is a deliberate design choice: a learned aggregator would face meta-circularity, as its own training data may be contaminated, precluding unbiased weight estimation. In Stage~2 (\emph{Contamination-Augmented 4PL IRT}), exposure scores enter a four-parameter logistic IRT model as covariates, with a global contamination effect parameter~$\gamma$ estimated jointly with item and ability parameters via Bayesian inference. A measurement error model treats the observed exposure scores as noisy proxies for latent contamination status, automatically propagating detection uncertainty into posterior estimates. Calibrated scores are obtained by setting exposure to zero and marginalizing over parameter uncertainty, producing point estimates with 50\%/80\%/95\% Bayesian credible intervals. Models trained via RL receive appropriately wider intervals, reflecting the genuine epistemic uncertainty that arises when detection signals are degraded.
tool_args.new_string: We propose ContamCal, a two-stage framework that provides both calibrated benchmark scores and domain-level contamination diagnosis. In Stage~1 (\emph{Multi-Signal Provenance Mapping}), four training-free detection signals---embedding-based near-duplicate retrieval, Min-K\%++ membership inference, ConStat performance gaps, and Self-Critique entropy collapse---are aggregated via reciprocal rank fusion \citep[RRF;][]{cormack2009} to produce per-item exposure scores. RRF is a deliberate design choice: a learned aggregator would face meta-circularity, as its own training data may be contaminated, precluding unbiased weight estimation. In Stage~2 (\emph{Contamination-Augmented IRT}), exposure scores enter an IRT model as covariates with per-domain contamination effect parameters~$\gamma_k$, estimated jointly with item and ability parameters via Bayesian inference. A measurement error model treats the observed exposure scores as noisy proxies for latent contamination status, automatically propagating detection uncertainty into posterior estimates. The framework delivers two distinct outputs: (a)~calibrated scores from the IRT ability estimates~$\theta_i$, obtained by marginalizing over posterior uncertainty with 50\%/80\%/95\% credible intervals; and (b)~domain-level contamination diagnosis from the~$\gamma_k$ parameters, revealing which cognitive domains are inflated, deflated, or unaffected. Empirically, we find that the calibration benefit arises from IRT ability estimation itself rather than from the explicit $\gamma$ correction, while $\gamma$ provides diagnostic information that aggregate metrics cannot capture. Models trained via RL receive appropriately wider intervals, reflecting the genuine epistemic uncertainty that arises when detection signals are degraded.

tool_args.old_string: Our contributions are organized hierarchically. At the core: (1)~the ContamCal framework itself---a two-stage pipeline comprising RRF-based provenance mapping and contamination-augmented 4PL IRT with per-benchmark contamination effects and a measurement error model for exposure---that produces calibrated benchmark scores with Bayesian credible intervals; (2)~a signal survival analysis demonstrating that contamination detection signals degrade in a cliff-like, rather than gradual, manner under RL post-training, yielding a signal~$\times$~regime AUC mapping with practical implications for the detection community; and (3)~dual-track validation through controlled SFT contamination injection across multiple model scales (0.5B--7B) within the Qwen2.5 family (internal validity) combined with an ecological RL case study (external validity). Supporting these core contributions: (4)~a simulation identifiability study grounded in Fisher information analysis, with a 144-condition sweep establishing minimum signal quality and model count thresholds for reliable parameter recovery; and (5)~comprehensive evaluation against seven baselines using five quantitative metrics---calibration MAE, credible interval coverage, interval sharpness, ranking preservation (Kendall's~$\tau$), and dose-response monotonicity---with bootstrap confidence intervals on all comparisons.

42	\begin{enumerate}
43	    \item[\textbf{B0.}] \textbf{Raw}: original benchmark scores with no adjustment, serving as the anchor for quantifying contamination inflation.

48	    \item[\textbf{B5.}] \textbf{Emperor's mitigation}: two representative strategies from \citet{xu2025emperor}---item rephrasing and option shuffling---applied at evaluation time. We report the better-performing strategy per benchmark.
49	    \item[\textbf{B6.}] \textbf{DCR}: the decontaminated calibration and ranking method of \citet{li2025dcr}, which produces adjusted accuracy via fuzzy inference over detection signals without uncertainty quantification.
